painting-mss.name: oil painting
painting-mss.title: oil painting
painting-mss.reason: The painting depicts a named Oglala (Lakota) chief, "War Eagle," wearing genuine Plains regalia — an eagle-feather war bonnet, ear ornament, beaded/fringed scalp shirt, and hide robe — consistent with Lakota material culture and dress, so it belongs to the claimed people despite being painted rather than photographed from life.

painting-mss.name: oil painting
painting-mss.title: oil painting
painting-mss.reason: A painted portrait of Red Cloud (Makhpiya-Luta), Oglala Lakota chief, shown in traditional fringed shirt, beaded/quilled pouch, blanket, and beaded strip — an authentic depiction of Lakota dress and regalia made and worn by the culture itself.

painting-mss.name: oil painting
painting-mss.title: oil painting
painting-mss.reason: The painting depicts a Brulé Lakota woman (wife of Spotted Tail) wearing traditional dress, earrings, decorated shawl, and jewelry — a portrait documenting Lakota attire, made by an outsider artist but depicting genuine Lakota material culture.

photo.name: photographic print; glass negative
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Red Shirt, an identified Oglala Lakota (Sioux) man, in full eagle-feather headdress, bone breastplate, fringed shirt and leggings — documentary photo of Lakota dress, matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of an Oohenonpa (Two Kettle Lakota/Teton Sioux) chief in traditional dress—feathered hat, shell ear ornaments, fringed jacket, fur blanket, embroidered leggings, moccasins, and tomahawk—directly documenting Lakota dress and regalia.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Lone Wolf, an Oglala Lakota man, in ornamented dress with ear ornaments, ribbon-wound hair, and a cross necklace, documenting Lakota dress and appearance. This is a documentary photo of the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of three Sioux (Brulé/Lakota) men in traditional dress—hairplate ornaments, conchos, military-style jacket, leggings, moccasins—standing beside a tipi with a camp in the background; clearly Plains Sioux material culture and dress.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Yellow Eagle, an Oglala Sioux (Lakota) man, wearing traditional dentalium/abalone ear ornaments, shell choker, hide tunic, and a quillwork-decorated blanket — a documentary photo of Lakota dress, matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; glass negative
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: The image shows Broken Arm, a Sioux (Lakota) chief, in profile wearing a feathered warbonnet, bone hairpipe breastplate, and fringed shirt — documentary portrait dress consistent with the claimed Lakota ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: A studio portrait of Big Foot (Che-tan-keah), a Miniconjou Lakota chief, in braided hair wrap and a choker/cross necklace, documenting Lakota dress and adornment — clear fit for the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Oohenonpa (Sioux/Lakota-related Teton) chief in traditional dress—fur/hide garment, moccasins, pipe, feathered hat—a documentary photo of dress and material culture consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Red Cloud, an Oglala Lakota chief, a documentary photograph of a member of the claimed people; his long hair and features are visible though he wears Western dress rather than Lakota regalia.

garment.name: skjorta, tunic, shirt
garment.title: skjorta, tunic, shirt
garment.reason: This is a hide war shirt with quillwork/beaded strips, hair-lock fringe, and characteristic V-neck bib design typical of Plains Sioux (Lakota/Oceti Sakowin) warrior regalia, matching the museum's attribution and provenance (taken at Yellowstone River, Montana/Wyoming).

garment.name: sko, mockasin, skodon, shoe, moccasins
garment.title: sko, mockasin, skodon, shoe, moccasins
garment.reason: A pair of beaded hide moccasins with typical Lakota/Sioux-style geometric beadwork in lazy-stitch, collected as part of the 1893 Retzius expedition to North America and catalogued as Lakota/Sioux — consistent with Plains Lakota footwear.

garment.name: pouch
garment.title: pouch
garment.reason: A quilled and beaded pouch with galloping-horse motif, fringed tassels with metal cones, matches Plains Lakota beadwork/quillwork craft traditions.

garment.name: vaate
garment.title: vaate
garment.reason: A tanned hide war-shirt (poncho-style men's shirt) with quilled shoulder/arm strips, fringe, and feather at the neck — a classic Plains war-shirt form consistent with Lakota dress.

garment.name: huvudprydnad, huvudbonad, feather headdress
garment.title: huvudprydnad, huvudbonad, feather headdress
garment.reason: An eagle-feather war bonnet with a beaded browband, a classic Plains/Lakota-type headdress, plausible for the claimed Lakota (Sioux) attribution and well within the known material culture of the region.

household.name: Ceremonial tobacco pouch
household.title: Ceremonial tobacco pouch
household.reason: The image shows a beaded and quilled hide pipe/tobacco bag with fringe, a classic Plains Lakota craft object, matching the museum's attribution to the Lakota ca. 1870-1880.

household.name: Tobacco pouch
household.title: Tobacco pouch
household.reason: A quilled/beaded hide tobacco pouch with fringe and geometric beadwork panel, consistent with Plains beadwork traditions including Lakota work; plausible object for this culture.

arms.name: rintapanssari
arms.title: rintapanssari
arms.reason: This is a hairpipe breastplate made of bone tube beads strung in rows with glass beads and claw ornaments — a classic Plains-style body armor/ornament of the type made and worn by Lakota and other Plains peoples for regalia and defense. It fits both the claimed ethnicity and category as arms/armor.
